title: gen_server Essentials: start_link, Synchronous call & Async cast
solutionExplanation: Implements synchronous call for debit/get_balances with backpressure and asynchronous cast for credit, maintaining an atomic multi-currency ledger map.

otpDocCards.description: Performs a synchronous call to ServerRef, waiting for a reply with a default 5000ms timeout.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Synchronous round-trip; provides natural flow-control backpressure.

otpDocCards.description: Sends an asynchronous message to ServerRef, returning ok immediately without waiting for a reply.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(1) non-blocking send; lacks natural backpressure.

mentalModelCheck.question: Under high traffic bursts, why is gen_server:call safer than gen_server:cast for processing operations?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
%% Cast: returns ok instantly, zero client wait
gen_server:cast(Server, {process_transaction, Tx})

%% Call: blocks caller until server replies
gen_server:call(Server, {process_transaction, Tx})

options.label: Call forces callers to wait for a reply, providing natural backpressure that prevents the server mailbox from overflowing into an Out-Of-Memory crash.
options.explanation: Correct! Callers cannot produce faster than the server consumes because each caller process is paused waiting for handle_call/3 to return.

options.label: Cast messages are encrypted, which consumes 10x more CPU cycles.
options.explanation: Cast messages are not encrypted; they are raw Erlang terms.

options.label: Call bypasses the server mailbox and writes directly to server memory.
options.explanation: Processes have completely isolated heaps; call still sends a message through the mailbox.
